## Scope and search provenance

This is a structured scoping review and evidence map of type 1 diabetes (T1D) games, not a registered systematic review. It includes education, self-management, coping and experiential games; mixed-diabetes, clinician-training, physical-game, exergame and gamified-utility comparators are labelled separately.

The inherited review reports independent database and product searches, backward references and forward citations through **24 August 2026**. [Nørlev et al. (2022; online 2021)](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34024156/) was a starting point for citation searching, not the sole inclusion boundary: its own search ended on 23 September 2020 and concerned children aged 8–14.

Reported routes include PubMed/PubMed Central, Crossref/OpenAlex, JMIR, ACM, IEEE Xplore, ClinicalTrials.gov, app stores and product/distribution sites. OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar were reported as forward-citation indexes. The [source register](references/SOURCE-INDEX.md) preserves query families, summary counts and the 18-article reference-list check.

**Reproducibility limitation:** complete historical exports, executed database-specific queries, deduplication records and individual screening decisions were not recovered. The reported search coverage and citation-index overlap therefore cannot be independently reconstructed. Historical counts are not presented as newly verified searches.

## Interpreting evidence

| Claim basis | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Direct evidence | A relevant T1D-game population and measured outcome |
| Adjacent evidence | A different disease, population or learning context |
| Industry practice | A documented production convention, not health-effect evidence |
| Design inference | A reasoned proposal requiring evaluation |
| Product claim | A developer or distributor statement, not an independently measured effect |
| Unknown | The relevant information was not verified |

The catalogue distinguishes controlled outcomes, uncontrolled change, feasibility, usability/co-design, development work and unevaluated products. These are navigation categories, not quality scores. **Study design and purpose are separate:** a feasibility study can be randomised. The [study register](data/studies.json) records tested versions, participants, denominators, outcomes, source-reading depth and appraisal concerns; empty fields indicate incomplete extraction.

Knowledge, competence, transfer, coping, engagement, behaviour and clinical outcomes are not interchangeable. The [evaluation chapter](knowledge/design/evaluation.qmd) maps each to suitable assessments.

## Product dates and access

The [catalogue](explorer.html) distinguishes release dates from study/report years; missing release dates remain unknown. Availability and prices are dated observations, not permanent attributes. Store visibility does not establish installation, regional completeness or operation on every supported device. All records remain **not playtested**.

Official, store, repository, trial and publication links have separate labels. A review mentioning a game is not a play link. Project-affiliated products use the same schema and evidence requirements as other games.

## Updates and remaining gaps

The targeted **6 September 2026** audit corrected selected claims and sources; it was not a comprehensive search or availability refresh. Adjacent reviews added then remain incompletely appraised, and unresolved candidates are listed in the [eligibility ledger](references/ELIGIBILITY-DECISIONS.md).

**15 September 2026:** DEXTRO DASH 2000 was added from a user nomination and developer documentation, without an outcome evaluation. Catalogue restructuring and editorial compression on that date do not refresh the scientific search, product verification or full-text appraisal dates.

**16 September 2026:** learning, evaluation and sustainability chapters were expanded through targeted source appraisal; a regulatory chapter was added from official guidance. Detailed physiology was restored from the corrected canonical physiological reference, with source-version and transfer records. This is not a comprehensive search update or independent verification of every transferred claim. The [source register](references/SOURCE-INDEX.md) links the chapter-specific records and unresolved access gaps.

Full-text limitations are recorded in the [wishlist](references/PAYWALLED-WISHLIST.md) and source ledgers. Acquisition, resource identity and scientific appraisal are distinct: retaining a file does not establish that every claim has been checked against it.

## Reference

[Nørlev, J. et al. (2022) ‘Game mechanisms in serious games that teach children with type 1 diabetes how to self-manage: A systematic scoping review’, *Journal of Diabetes Science and Technology*, 16(5), pp. 1253–1269.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34024156/)
